info.title: LibreEcho Device API
info.description: Local administration API shared by the mock and Linux hardware backends. State-changing requests require X-LibreEcho-CSRF. Device power operations also require X-LibreEcho-Confirm.

get.summary: Read voice-assistant state and latency telemetry
get.description: Reports subscription authentication, wake/STT stream health, and measured speech-end-to-first-PCM latency.

put.description: Configures ChatGPT or an OpenAI-compatible local endpoint, model, voice-safe instruction prompt, and whether wake-to-reply is enabled. API keys are write-only and never returned.

base_url.description: Configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint, usually ending in /v1

get.summary: Read the bounded device-side voice turn history
get.description: Returns up to 12 newest device-measured turns plus a persisted history_generation. The history ring is persisted by agentd and restored after restart; clients should discard cached rows when history_generation changes, but may preserve them when an empty response has the same generation.

post.description: Polls at the server-provided interval and stores successful OAuth credentials in the device's private persistent secret store.
Returns a verification URL and user code. LibreEcho does not request an OpenAI API key.
Deletes the locally stored OAuth credentials and disables authenticated requests until device login is completed again.

post.summary: Stream a text request into spoken playback
post.description: Sends text through the configured subscription provider, segments streamed response text at voice-safe boundaries, and queues it on the local announcement bus.

get.description: Returns available audio state. On images without audiod, the 200 response contains data.available=false and data.unavailable=true; this is an expected capability result, not an HTTP error.

put.summary: Update volume, microphone state, or announcement voice

post.summary: Speak an announcement through the local speaker
post.description: Queues text for the warm local TTS service. Audio is streamed into audiod's priority announcement bus so external local services do not need direct hardware access.

post.summary: Speak a phrase into the microphone path
post.description: Renders the phrase with the device's own text-to-speech and plays it into the capture path, so wake-word detection, speech-to-text and the assistant process it as though it had been spoken in the room. Intended for testing. Nothing is recorded and nothing leaves the device.
Plays one raw sound from the installed sound directory. Names are lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, or underscores and are limited to 48 characters. Other HTTP methods return 405.

post.summary: Create the first local administrator account
post.description: Available only when the configured users file is absent or empty. The first successful request wins and immediately enables user authentication.

post.summary: Invalidate the current local user session

get.description: Returns the Echo 9-lane transport endpoint, the seven verified microphone lanes, and the seven-entry logical miccal contract. Values are read from /proc/idme/miccal.* with 16384 as the fallback. Raw browser monitoring does not apply logical gains until physical geometry ordering is verified; audio is never recorded.

Streams microphone audio at 16 kHz using HTTP chunked transfer encoding. When the wake-word service is running, the endpoint subscribes to its shared calibrated mono stream (pcm_s16_le, one channel) so baby monitoring does not open a second ALSA capture. If wake-word is unavailable, it falls back to the selected verified raw microphone lane using the 9-channel packed signed 24-bit little-endian PCM container (pcm_s24_3le) carrying sign-extended 16-bit samples; lanes 7 and 8 are inactive or reserved. The source query value is card:device and channel selects 0 through 6. Authentication is applied when enabled.

200.description: Chunked PCM audio; format is declared by X-LibreEcho-Audio

get.summary: Read Bluetooth controller, discovery, pairing, bond and profile-service state
get.description: The response separates controller protocol capabilities from registered userspace profile services. Kernel RFCOMM, BNEP, or HIDP support alone does not make a profile service available. profile_state is pairing-only until SDP/profile services are installed and supervised. When the controller adapter is absent, the 200 response contains data.available=false and data.unavailable=true. The response includes address (live HCI address), address_factory (board-recorded address when available), and address_configured (persisted override; empty means no override).

put.summary: Enable Bluetooth or update discoverable/connectable settings

post.summary: Start pairing with a discovered or known device
Enter or leave pairing mode and make the controller visible
Answer a pending confirmation, passkey or PIN request
Start a Classic + LE discovery scan
post.description: Starting a scan clears the previous discovery results, so the discovered array in the immediate response is empty. The scan then finishes on its own when the controller's inquiry period ends: poll GET /api/v1/bluetooth until scanning is false, at which point discovered holds the devices this scan found. Returns 409 when the controller is not enabled.

post.summary: Remove a paired device and its stored bond

get.summary: Read button settings and live physical-input capability state
get.description: Returns saved tones/action/brightness settings plus live capability fields from libreecho-buttond. `available` is true only for a fresh connected status record; `stale` is true when the record is missing, disconnected, or older than 15 seconds. The response data includes `short_press`, `long_press`, `tones`, `action`, `action_sounds`, `available_sounds`, `action_brightness`, `mute_brightness`, `volume_capable`, `hardware_mute`, and `action_capable`. Sound names are lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, or underscores and are at most 48 characters each; an empty `action_sounds` is valid and disables sound playback.

put.summary: Update button mappings, cues, action, and brightness
put.description: All supplied fields are validated before applying the update. `tones` is a boolean; `action` is one of `sound`, `listen`, `playpause`, or `disabled`; `action_sounds` is a comma-separated rotation list of lowercase sound names, each 1–48 characters; `action_brightness` and `mute_brightness` are integers from 0 through 100. Malformed or out-of-range fields return 400.

get.description: Returns the compile-time LibreEcho OS version alongside authentication and request metadata. The os_version value is sourced from the release VERSION file during the daemon build.

post.summary: Validate, apply and persist portable configuration

label.description: Optional label; its UTF-8 encoding must be no longer than 47 bytes and must not contain control characters.

delete.summary: Cancel a pending timer; use dismiss for ringing timers

get.summary: Read device identity and audio capability
get.description: Identity plus an optional `audio` object describing capture, output and streaming capability. `audio` and every member of it are optional: older daemons omit it and the mock backend does not synthesize one, so clients render what is present. An empty `audio.streaming.decoders` means the device cannot decode compressed streams itself; `audio.streaming.available` lists the transports that deliver already-decoded audio.

get.summary: List a USB drive attached to the OTG port
get.description: Reports the attached USB disk and lists one directory of it. Optional `path` query selects a directory relative to the mount; it is limited to 255 bytes and rejected if any component is `.` or `..`, contains a backslash or starts with a slash, so a listing can never escape the drive. Ordinary names containing consecutive dots are allowed. Answers `size_bytes`, `used_bytes` and `free_bytes` from statvfs, plus `rel_path` echoing the directory listed. `present` is false when the port is in device mode or no disk is attached; `mounted` is false when a disk is present but no filesystem could be mounted. The drive is mounted read-only, nosuid and nodev.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Directory relative to the drive root; path components `.` and `..`, backslashes and leading slashes are rejected. Names containing consecutive dots are valid.

post.summary: Play an audio file from the USB drive
post.description: Body is `{"path":"..."}` relative to the drive root. The path is refused if any component is `.` or `..`, contains a backslash or a leading slash; ordinary names containing consecutive dots are allowed, so playback cannot escape the mount. Only `.mp3` is accepted: radiod decodes MPEG-1/2 Layer III and this image carries no AAC decoder, so other audio formats answer `415` with that reason rather than starting and staying silent. Playback runs through the same radiod path as internet radio, so `/integrations/radio/stop` stops it.

path.description: File path relative to the USB drive root; it must name an existing regular `.mp3` file. Path components `.` and `..`, backslashes and leading slashes are rejected; names containing consecutive dots are valid.

get.description: Returns the tail of the kernel ring buffer as `lines`, most recent last, with `count`. Bounded to the last 80 records. Drained non-blocking from /dev/kmsg. This exists because switching the USB port to host mode removes the ADB gadget, which is the device's only shell, making the kernel log unreadable over USB at exactly the moment it is needed; this endpoint reads it over the network instead.

Streams the complete dmesg output as a text/plain attachment using chunked transfer encoding. The response is raw log text rather than the JSON envelope. Kernel-log access failures return the standard JSON error envelope with HTTP 503 before any success headers are sent. At most four kernel-log workers run concurrently.

post.description: Authenticated action returning a bounded, deterministic-ordered JSON diagnostic bundle. It includes public-safe release identity and available runtime, network, audio, wake-word, Bluetooth, playback, privacy, reset/pstore-summary and bounded log evidence. Wi-Fi credentials, SSID/BSSID, IP/MAC/Bluetooth addresses, owner identifiers, tokens, private paths, media metadata, signing material and raw pstore are omitted or redacted. Missing or malformed subsystem data is represented as unavailable without failing the export.

get.description: Returns whether the Spotify Connect daemon is installed in the image, whether it is enabled, whether it is playing, the device name shown in Spotify, and its current status. The device name is escaped as JSON and may contain quotes or backslashes. This endpoint is read-only; unsupported methods, including HEAD, receive 405.

The `rest` item is the canonical LAN REST API state. Its `enabled` value mirrors effective LAN exposure and its `forced` value reports the development-only bind override; when forced, the corresponding UI control is read-only.

Returns `max_stations`, `playback_supported`, the live `playing` / `playing_url` pair and the `stations` array. `playback_supported` is answered by asking radiod rather than by a constant: an image without a stream player reports false, and a client should say so rather than implying playback works. `playing` is radiod's own state and is the authoritative answer to whether a stream is running; `playing_url` is empty when it is not.

put.summary: Replace the internet radio station list
put.description: Replaces the whole list. The request body is flat and numbered rather than an array: the daemon reads JSON scalars by key and has no array parser. For every index i below `station_count`, send `station_i_word` and `station_i_url`, optionally `station_i_name` and `station_i_enabled`. The response is the stored list in the same shape as GET. Validation failures answer 400 with a message describing the rule that was broken.

station_0_word.description: What the station is asked for by. Lowercase letters, digits, spaces and hyphens; no leading or trailing space; unique across the list.

station_0_name.description: Display name. Defaults to the word when blank or absent.

station_0_url.description: Stream URL. Printable ASCII with no spaces.

post.description:
Starts the station whose `word` matches, by its stored URL. Answers 404 when no station has that word, 409 when the station exists but is switched off, and 501 when the image has no stream player. The response is the station list in the same shape as GET, so `playing` and `playing_url` come back with it.

The assistant does not reach this: agentd has no radio path, so a spoken request for a station cannot start one. Playback is started over the API today.

word.description: The stored word of the station to play.

post.description:
Stops whatever radiod is playing. Stopping a stream that is already stopped is not an error, so this is safe to send unconditionally as cleanup. Answers 501 when the image has no stream player. The response is the station list in the same shape as GET.

This is the only way to stop the radio today: agentd has no radio path, so "stop" spoken over the music does not reach radiod.

get.description: Returns available LED state. On images without ledd, the 200 response contains data.available=false and data.unavailable=true.

put.summary: Update LED colour, brightness or music visualizer preference

put.description: Night mode caps the ring to a dim theme on a local-time schedule. Because the schedule is local, the device timezone must be correct.

get.summary: Read association, gateway liveness, and recovery state

put.summary: Update hostname, local access, and persistent MAC overrides

get.summary: Scan Wi-Fi networks with radio metadata and security capabilities
get.description: Returns distinct SSIDs ordered with 5 GHz preferred, then descending signal strength and a stable SSID tie-breaker. Each result preserves frequency_mhz, channel, band, RSSI in rssi_dbm, advertised security capabilities, and whether an explicit WPA2 attempt is appropriate. WPA3/SAE-advertised networks remain visible; the response is bounded to the first 12 distinct results for the fixed adapter message size.

200.description: Each network includes frequency_mhz, channel, band, rssi_dbm, capabilities, and wpa2_attempt; security distinguishes wpa3-transition from wpa3-only.

get.summary: Read unified playback source, priority-bus state, media metadata and what the transport can do
get.description:
metadata.station is the station name when internet radio is playing: the name from the stored station list when the URL matches one, otherwise the stream's own icy-name. metadata.title for radio is the ICY StreamTitle the station interleaved into the stream, and is null when the station sends none -- no title is invented from the URL.

transport reports what this device can actually do to whatever is playing: {play, pause, stop, reason}. pause is always false. A live radio stream has no buffered position to resume from, so radiod can only stop and reconnect; AirPlay and Bluetooth playback is driven by the phone that started it (airplayd exposes status and an enable switch only, and the Bluetooth stack here is an AVRCP target, which answers transport commands and cannot send them). reason is the sentence to show beside a control that is disabled.

post.summary: Start or stop what is playing
post.description:
Body is {"action":"play"|"pause"|"stop"}. The successful response is the same document as GET /api/v1/playback, taken after the action.

"stop" stops internet radio. "play" starts the last station started in this session again -- a fresh connection that rejoins the broadcast live, not a resume. That station is held in memory only and is forgotten on restart, so after a reboot there is nothing to start again.

"pause" is accepted and answered 501 with the reason rather than rejected as an unknown action: no source on this device can be paused. Read the transport block from GET /api/v1/playback before offering a control, so a button that cannot work is disabled with its reason instead of failing when pressed.

get.description: Reports explicit microphone retention mode (`audio_retention_mode`: none, local, or remote), bounded duration and size cap (`audio_retention_hours`, `audio_retention_max_mb`), and the remote destination state. Remote retention reports unavailable and has effective_mode=none until an authenticated HTTPS transport is present; it never falls back to local storage.

put.description: State-changing requests require CSRF. audio_retention is none, local, or remote (legacy 24h is accepted as local). Remote mode requires an HTTPS URL without embedded credentials; credentials are supplied out of band and are never exported.

get.description: Returns the OS version, source commit, clean/dirty source flag, and content digest embedded at build time.
Returns safe initial values, boot-time owner-local firmware import state, live wlan0 registration, and whether first-boot setup is complete. Wi-Fi credentials are never returned.

post.description: Validates and applies hostname, Wi-Fi, audio, wake-word and privacy basics, then requests access-point handoff. Hostname, audio, Wi-Fi and persistence failures return stage-specific errors. After the settings and Wi-Fi commit, the daemon synchronously invokes the no-argument `/usr/local/sbin/libreecho-reconcile-features` helper and waits for `/run/libreecho/startup-ready` before completing setup. Reconciliation or readiness failure returns 503 and leaves setup incomplete; if and only if the optional wake adapter reports not-supported, setup continues and persists wake_word and wake_sensitivity for later restore. This one-time operation is rejected after setup completes.

get.description: Returns TSL2540 ambient-light telemetry. `available` is false when no usable sensor is present; in that case the other readings are not meaningful. `lux` and `calibrated_lux` may be zero for a dark room. `bus` reports the actual detected I²C device, such as `i2c 0-0039` or `i2c 1-0039`.

Returns CPU, memory, storage, temperature, and ambient-light telemetry. `light_lux` is the current ambient-light reading in lux, or `-1` when no usable sensor is present; `0` is a valid dark-room reading.

get.summary: Read OS, NTP and PMIC RTC state
get.description: Reports whether network time has synchronized, the configured public peers, the last successful synchronization, and whether UTC was persisted to the hardware RTC.

post.description: Permanently removes every file and nested directory below the product image's /data/libreecho/config and /data/libreecho/secrets directories, including accounts, setup completion, Wi-Fi profiles and PSKs, assistant credentials, timers, and all mutable user configuration. The reset synchronizes both persistent directories and reboots. Installed feature payloads, OTA artifacts, and release identity outside those directories are preserved. Unprivileged Linux deployments return 501 without deleting state.

get.description: Optional features are off by default. `simulation` enables POST /audio/simulate; while it is off that endpoint answers 403 and the web interface hides its Simulation page. `usb_host` reports whether the OTG port is currently in host mode, `usb_role` is the raw role read back from the kernel, and `usb_role_supported` is false on images or hardware without a switchable role.

put.summary: Switch an optional feature on or off
put.description: Send `simulation` to change the persisted feature switch. Send `usb_host` to move the OTG port between host mode (reads an attached USB drive) and device mode (serves ADB); the port cannot do both at once. `usb_host` is applied immediately and is deliberately NOT persisted -- every boot pins the port back to device mode so the ADB recovery path can never be left switched off by a stored setting. Returns 501 when the running kernel exposes no switchable USB role. The response is the new feature state.

simulation.description: Play rendered speech into the microphone path for testing wake word, speech-to-text and the assistant.

usb_host.description: Switch the OTG port immediately between host/storage mode and device/ADB mode. This live setting is not persisted and resets to device mode on reboot.

put.description: A POSIX TZ string such as CST6CDT,M3.2.0,M11.1.0. There is no zoneinfo database on the device, so Olson names are not accepted. Daemons read TZ at start, so the change applies after a restart.

get.summary: Read signed A/B update and source-check state
get.description: Reports installed and latest verified versions, GitHub Release reachability, check timestamps and errors, pending activation, slots, rollback state, and whether the installed update helper supports unsigned manual uploads. Also reports the two OTA upload sizes: `max_upload_ceiling_bytes` (33554432, i.e. 32 MiB), the fixed limit POST /system/update/upload always refuses above, and `max_upload_bytes`, that ceiling capped by the free space on the filesystem the package is staged to, less a margin for the installer. Clients should read `max_upload_bytes` rather than hard-coding a number; when it is below the ceiling, free space is the binding limit. The size of the image already installed in a slot is not reported.

post.summary: Download, verify and install the available update
post.description: Requires a successful check reporting an available release, uses the same signed A/B installer as manual uploads, and does not restart the device.

put.summary: Enable or disable automatic signed update installation
put.description: Automatic installation is disabled by default and never restarts the device.

put.summary: Select the signed OTA update channel

post.summary: Check GitHub Releases for a signed update
Stream a LibreEcho OTA tar to the inactive slot
post.description: Manual uploads are signature-verified by default. The optional X-LibreEcho-Allow-Unsigned header is honored only when GET /api/v1/system/update reports allow_unsigned=true; it applies only to this manually selected package and bypasses signature verification. A body over `max_upload_ceiling_bytes`, or over the smaller `max_upload_bytes` this device can stage, is refused with 413 before the body is read; the second case names the device's own limit.

get.summary: Read speech pipeline configuration and endpoint health
get.description: Reports local or remote speech recognition and synthesis engines, configured Wyoming endpoints, reachability, the on-device wake-word stage, persisted listening settings, and the state of the latest bounded voice-pipeline restart. `restart.state` is `ready`, `pending`, or `failed`; `restart.error` is non-empty when the last restart failed. max_utterance_ms is 2000–20000, end_silence_ms is 200–3000, and vad_floor_rms is 1–1024.

200.description: Speech pipeline and persisted listening settings

put.summary: Configure and activate the speech pipeline
put.description: Persists and applies local, custom, or Home Assistant mode. Custom mode uses remote Wyoming Whisper and Piper services while wake-word detection remains on-device. When daemon init scripts are present, activation is bounded to one restart job: the successful response is 202 with `restart.state: pending`; concurrent updates return 409 until it completes. Poll GET /api/v1/voice-pipeline for `restart.state` and `restart.error`; asynchronous restart failures are reported as 503 on the next PUT and remain visible in GET state.

get.description: Returns available wake-word state. On images without the wake-word service, the 200 response contains data.available=false and data.unavailable=true.

Csrf.name: X-LibreEcho-CSRF
Csrf.description: Use the 64-character token returned by GET /api/v1/config; it changes on daemon boot.

AllowUnsigned.name: X-LibreEcho-Allow-Unsigned
AllowUnsigned.description: Set to 1 only for a manually selected package when GET /api/v1/system/update reports allow_unsigned=true. Bypasses signature verification for that upload; fetched and automatic updates never honor it.

NetworkUpdate.description: Updates hostname, local access, or persistent MAC overrides. MAC values must be six hexadecimal octets separated by colons or hyphens and must be unicast.

WifiConnect.description: Wi-Fi credentials. `security` accepts exactly `open` or `wpa2`; when omitted it defaults to `wpa2`. WPA3/SAE is not supported by the shipped MT8163 WEXT path.

NetworkState.description: Association and independently verified gateway-liveness state

gateway_reachable.description: Null until a probe can be completed

wifi_mac.description: Current Wi-Fi MAC address, or empty when unavailable

wifi_mac_factory.description: Factory Wi-Fi MAC from board identity data, or empty when unavailable

wifi_mac_configured.description: Persisted Wi-Fi MAC override, or empty when unset

bt_mac.description: Current Bluetooth MAC address, or empty when unavailable

bt_mac_factory.description: Factory Bluetooth MAC from board identity data, or empty when unavailable

bt_mac_configured.description: Persisted Bluetooth MAC override, or empty when unset

reason.description: Sanitized installer reason token when an OTA update is rejected
